result.stdout:
Description:
  Quest Viva command-line tools

Usage:
  qv [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  play <game>                Play a game in the terminal
  serve                      Play a game over a JSON-lines protocol on stdin/stdout, for programs to drive
  mcp <game>                 Run an MCP server over stdio whose tools play a game, for AI agents
  walkthrough <game> <name>  Run a game's built-in walkthroughs, exiting non-zero if any fails, for example in CI
  check <game>               Find problems in a game's scripts without playing it, exiting non-zero if there are any, for example in CI
  publish <game>             Publish a game, with the files in its folder, after checking it for problems
  preview <game>             Play a game in your browser, served by qv on this computer only, reloading it when its files change

result.stdout:
Description:
  Run an MCP server over stdio whose tools play a game, for AI agents

Usage:
  qv mcp [<game>] [options]

Arguments:
  <game>  The game to serve. Without one, the agent loads games with start_game

Options:
  --seed <seed>   Seed the game's random numbers, so the same commands give the same results
  --text-only     Give the agent only the game's text, without the exits a browser player sees in the compass
  --debug-tools   Also offer tools for debugging and fixing a game, which reach past what a player can do, such as evaluate, check and docs
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Run a game's built-in walkthroughs, exiting non-zero if any fails, for example in CI

Usage:
  qv walkthrough <game> [<name>] [options]

Arguments:
  <game>  The game to play: a .quest or .aslx file, or an .asl or .cas file from Quest 4 or earlier
  <name>  The walkthrough to run. Without one, every walkthrough runs, each from a fresh start

Options:
  --seed <seed>   Seed the game's random numbers (default 1234, so every run gives the same results)
  --quiet         Print only whether each walkthrough passed, not its transcript
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Publish a game, with the files in its folder, after checking it for problems

Usage:
  qv publish <game> [options]

Arguments:
  <game>  The game to publish: an .aslx file

Options:
  --format <format>            What to make, as the Editor's Publish does: quest, a .quest package; html, one web page that loads the player from jsDelivr (a released qv only); or zip, the page and the player for any web host [default: quest]
  -o, --output <output>        Where to write it. By default, beside the game: game.aslx makes game.quest, game.html or game-html.zip
  --force                      Publish even if qv check finds problems in the game
  --player <player>            For --format zip, use the WasmPlayer bundle in this folder instead of the one built into qv
  --cdn-version <cdn-version>  For --format html, load the player from jsDelivr at this published version instead of qv's own
  -?, -h, --help               Show help and usage information

Description:
  Play a game in your browser, served by qv on this computer only, reloading it when its files change

Usage:
  qv preview <game> [options]

Arguments:
  <game>  The game to preview: usually an .aslx file, but any game the player can play

Options:
  --port <port>      The port to serve on. By default, a free one
  --seed <seed>      Seed the game's random numbers, so the same commands give the same results
  --player <player>  Serve the WasmPlayer bundle in this folder instead of the one built into qv
  -?, -h, --help     Show help and usage information
